claim: Sensemaking is a two-way fit (data into frame, frame around data); a current frame selects and connects data, and poor fit triggers revision. Stated by Klein and repeated in all secondary sources, but the primary texts (2006, 2007) were not opened by any agent. Gap 5 stays open: the 2006 paper was confirmed to exist (Crossref, 395 citing works) but not readable (d22).
agent_test: Compare an S2 that stores frame plus anchors and re-fits against a flat list of rules, at equal tokens, on items with a located failing output.

claim: In the one direct lab test on structure tasks (11 people, 44 tasks), people kept a single frame in 44 of 44 tasks; the claim of up to three parallel frames was not seen. Recognising the problem and building a frame came before data search. Candidate answers were 'frame instantiations'. Re-verified in the paper. Gap search 2026-11-03: the one LLM test of keeping K hypotheses (Gemini, d02) was model dependent (Pro 4.7 to 19.1% from K=1 to 5; Flash 22.6 to 5.0%), so more frames help only with arbitration.
agent_test: Run S2 with 1 frame vs 3 parallel frames at equal tokens; also test frame-first vs data-first ordering.

claim: Experts differ from novices by using prior knowledge as soft evidence, elaborating the frame more, checking source credibility more and discarding more data; novices want hard evidence and finish shorter journeys (example only: E2 15 data points vs N6 6).
agent_test: Give the agent a library of prior frames from S9 memory vs none; measure first-pass rate at equal tokens.

claim: Early or wrong frames persist: the evidence needed to overturn an interpretation exceeds that needed to form it (Heuer; Bruner and Potter ordering effect). Numbers for the classic human studies were not recorded in this series.
agent_test: Plant a misleading first cue; measure how often the agent drops the first frame, with and without code-shuffled cue order in S2.

claim: LLMs show frame fixation in multi-turn input: 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulated conversations, average drop of 39% from full to sharded input; aptitude falls about 15-16% but unreliability rises 112%; the same text concatenated scores 95.1% of full, so it is not information loss. Models guess early and build on the guess. Re-verified.
agent_test: Feed cues in pieces vs all at once; measure the drop. Test a code-held 'all cues so far' restatement at equal tokens.

claim: Restating all prior cues each turn recovers only part of the multi-turn loss (Snowball about 15-20%, two models); low temperature leaves about 30% unreliability; reasoning models (o3, R1) degrade as much as others. Gap search: a code-side rebuild of the spec from user messages only (AC3) closes 55-84% of the gap to an oracle on 3 of 4 tasks, while a model summary does not (d05, d06).
agent_test: Same-paper claim. Test on our agent with a code-built cue ledger rather than a model recap.

claim: Without an external signal, LLM self-revision does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; GPT-3.5 kept its GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time. With oracle labels it gains (GPT-3.5 CSQA 89.7, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0), so earlier gains came from the oracle. Re-verified in the paper tables. Corroborated by Tyen 2024 and Reflexion needing a success signal. Nuance from gap search: when NEW evidence arrives, revision pays (MINT: up to 10.6x more wrong-to-right than right-to-wrong, d08); the harm is blind self-review.
agent_test: Reframe only after located failing output (G2) vs reframe on request; count right-to-wrong flips at equal tokens.

claim: Models can fix an error once its location is given but cannot find it: BIG-Bench Mistake GPT-4 step-level finding 52.87% direct; backtracking with oracle location raised originally wrong traces by +18 to +44 points. Reflexion works where an external success signal exists (ALFWorld 130/134) and gave no gain where it is weak (WebShop).
agent_test: Compare S5 given code-located failures against model-located failures at equal tokens.

claim: When a clinical decision needs more data, frontier LLMs anchor on the first diagnosis and stop looking: 32 models, 20 hematology cases; data requested fell from 56.8% (round 1) to 25.7% (round 3); 65.6% of 323 wrong or partial round-1 diagnoses stayed wrong (34.4% recovery); 50.8% of 307 correct round-1 diagnoses became wrong. Re-verified.
agent_test: Multi-round cue-requesting task: measure data requested per round and recovery; test a code-forced 'request one disconfirming cue' step.

claim: LLM reasoning traces commit early to the final answer: 36% of traces commit before halfway and 61% before three quarters; 96.1% put top probability on the diagnosis they finally give; later text lists alternatives without changing the outcome. Not re-opened (NeurIPS 2026 page).
agent_test: Probe our agent's commitment point mid-trace; compare with several short independent attempts.

claim: LLM premature closure: when the correct option is removed, five frontier models still pick an answer (false-action about 70% baseline, 48% with a safety prompt; MedQA n=500, AfriMed-QA n=490; HealthBench 861 questions 20.7-44.6% closure). A prompt reduces but does not remove it. Re-verified.
agent_test: Add a 'no frame fits' flag at S2 and check whether the agent uses it; measure the tension with G6 never-abstain. The two ids are the same paper, so counted as one source.

claim: LLMs are anchored by early information: SynAnchors 22-61% of questions anchored (Qwen2.5-0.5B 60.5%, GPT-4o 27.3%, DeepSeek-R1 25.0%, Qwen3-235B thinking 22.0%). Common mitigations did not remove it; reasoning helped most. Echterhoff 2024 and Valencia-Clavijo 2025 also find anchoring. Table values re-verified.
agent_test: Present cues in code-randomised order vs fixed order; check the anchoring gap.

claim: Narrative voice changes LLM diagnosis from the same facts: 12 open models, 1000 MedQA vignettes, accuracy 0.635 clinical voice vs 0.546 and 0.531 other voices; rewriting into clinical voice helped most. Separately, telling a model the wanted conclusion shifts its data analysis (14 models, 2,160 responses). Different tasks, neither tests frames.
agent_test: S1 restate into neutral form (input hygiene) vs raw; measure accuracy gap across voices.

claim: Abandoned interpretations leave residue in LLMs: 24 open models (124M-70B) after garden-path sentences carry about three quarters of the true-object effect; a corrected statement still pulls later predictions. Abstract re-checked on arXiv. Gap search: residue after a clarification is also measured in dialogue (Gemini 2.5, coding contamination 0.256) and an explicit rollback and rebuild cut it to 0.000 in a small test (d01, d03).
agent_test: After a reframe, start a fresh context without the abandoned frame vs keep it; compare.

claim: LLMs lean toward confirming tests: on the 2-4-6 rule task 11 LLMs mostly test confirming cases; counterexample prompts raised rule discovery from 42% to 56%. A rival paper argues positive tests are not simply a flaw (information-maximising queries fail when invalid programs are proposed).
agent_test: Ask the agent to generate disconfirming test inputs; compare discovery with confirming-only tests.

claim: LLMs fail at updating a conclusion when a premise changes: Belief-R (1,912 items; GPT-4 Turbo update accuracy 16.76%, maintain 86.72%, re-verified); chain-of-thought gives about 1 point; DeltaLogic small-model revision accuracy below first-pass (Qwen3-1.7B 0.667 to 0.467). BeliefShift shows retrieval helps revision (GPT-4o 0.71 to 0.83) on opinion-type beliefs.
agent_test: Edit one premise or cue in a solved item; measure whether S5/O8 revises, vs inertia.

claim: Tools built on the sensemaking-loop idea report gains for human users: Narrative Scaffolding N=20 alternatives considered 8.75 vs 3.25, time per insight 2.31 vs 4.62 min (re-verified); Sensecape N=12 concepts explored 68.3 vs 22.8; GLOSS 87.93% accuracy on 60 objective queries; LLM-augmented evidence trees F1 about 0.80 vs 0.65 clustering. These are system comparisons, not tests of the theory.
agent_test: Only the idea of forcing a list of rival frames transfers; test 'name 2 rival frames' at S2 vs one frame at equal tokens.

claim: No study found tests data-frame predictions (frame count, anchoring, reframing) on an LLM agent directly; the nearest are Braitsch (information seeking), Laban (fixation) and Pontis (humans, single frame). Absence is from a limited search. Gap search found only analogues in puzzle or code settings (Only Connect red herrings, Mini-ARC hypothesis mixing, SWE-Bench evolving intent); still no direct data-frame test.
agent_test: Our own experiment would be the first direct test.

claim: The data-frame authors' successor, the plausibility transition model, is case-based (73 cases, 23 analysed by one coder, no experiments): stop when the story is plausible enough. This follows Weick's plausibility over accuracy.
agent_test: Plausibility stopping vs check-based stopping (G3, G10): measure confident wrong answers.

claim: Written reasoning is a poor check on the frame: 91.1% of 17-model evaluations scored 6+ on a reasoning rubric (mean 8.22) while mean accuracy was 56.3%; reasoning traces commit early and keep listing alternatives.
agent_test: Compare rubric-pass rate to answer correctness in our logs.

claim: An ACT-R model with chunks as data frames reproduced four human biases (confirmation, anchoring, representativeness, probability matching) on six IARPA tasks without a bias module; no LLM equivalent was found.
agent_test: Not directly testable; suggests blended retrieval produces anchoring.

claim: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses reduced confirmation bias only for people without intelligence experience (MITRE 2008, from a search summary, PDF blocked). Analyst early-commitment (Tolcott 1989) and consider-the-opposite (Lord 1984) are recalled from background and unopened.
agent_test: Do not rely until opened.

claim: A formal data-frame loop exists: evidence extraction, hypothesis retrieval, scoring s(E,h) in [0,1], pick the argmax subject to threshold tau (Zheng 2025, prototype only, no user study). A 2026 position paper adds premise status (draft, contested, committed, rejected). Both are theory with no measured results.
agent_test: Implement frames as records with status; test status tracking vs plain text at equal tokens.

claim: A model's own recap or summary of the conversation does not cure fixation, but a user-only rebuild of the task spec does: AC3 reset reached 75.7% vs 56.1% full context (database, n=107) while a faithful condenser got 53.3% and flagged an assistant error in 0 of 340 summaries; Mem0 and summaries added about 1 to 3 points (53.6 to 54.7/56.5) against 73.9 for a rewrite into explicit instructions; 62.5% of summaries collapsed ambiguity.
agent_test: Compare a code-held ledger built only from user and tool facts, then fresh-context rebuild, against a model recap, at equal tokens.

claim: Revision is net helpful when new evidence arrives and a hold-before-commit option exists: in 1,035 diagnosis cases, over 55% of first answers came in the first two turns, 18.5% of them wrong, and incorrect-to-correct revisions ran up to 10.6x the correct-to-incorrect rate; deferring the question raised first-commitment accuracy by up to 62.6%.
agent_test: Add a code-forced 'name the missing cue and fetch it' step before first commitment; measure first-answer accuracy and abstain rate (must stay zero).

claim: A plausible rival story causes false revisions: handing a model a coherent argument for a wrong option made it drop a correct answer 17.5% to 97.3% of the time (mean 48.7%; 55.7% if attributed to itself). A reframe triggered by model-written counter-arguments will therefore flip right answers unless a tool or code check confirms the conflict.
agent_test: Measure right-to-wrong flip rate of O8 with trigger = located failure only vs trigger = model-judged cue conflict.

claim: Agreement across runs is not a check of the frame: step-4 hidden-state similarity predicts trajectory stability (r=-0.35) but correct and confidently wrong questions overlap, the effect vanishes on hard questions, and a commitment prompt did not improve accuracy (0.908 vs 0.923 control); a model can fix its answer before reasoning and keep it under a 4,096-token thinking budget (85-100% wrong).
agent_test: Do not use sample agreement as the stop or reframe test. Log whether the conclusion precedes the premise check.

claim: Listing more rival hypotheses is not enough: LLMs asked for sets of valid explanations show mode collapse (high validity, falling uniqueness and recovery as the space grows), and naive multi-hypothesis prompting gave the highest old-hypothesis contamination (1.029 vs 0.177 for raw history). Rivals need forced diversity and arbitration.
agent_test: Test 1 frame vs 2 frames with a forced differing cue and a code-side scoring step vs 2 unscored frames, at equal tokens.

claim: Fixation on a prior pattern shows in LLMs on trap tasks: GPT-4 10-shot solved 6 of 494 Only Connect walls vs 59 when red herrings were removed; most LLMs scored under 50% on mARC in early 2025 (physicians 66%) but by 2026 top reasoning models matched or beat physicians (Claude 4.1 Opus 0.75; 55-70% on physician-miss items); in MedEinst strong models ignore the key cue in over 35% of GPT-5 errors. Single-shot fixation is partly cured by reasoning; sequential fixation is not.
agent_test: Evaluate the scaffold on sequential tasks (cue arrives after commitment), where reasoning alone does not help.

claim: Classic human basis for early-frame stickiness is thin in our files: Bruner and Potter 1964 (later recognition after longer initial blur) and Lord, Lepper and Preston 1984 (consider-the-opposite beat 'be unbiased') were seen as abstracts only, with no sample sizes; Tolcott 1989 and Lehner 2008 were not readable.
agent_test: Treat the human findings as direction only; do not quote effect sizes.
